intro: «Aunque» can be «although» or «even if». The verb mood and the context show how you see it.
p.aunque.consejo: With the indicative it presents a fact; with the subjunctive, a possibility: «aunque llueva, saldré».
p.a pesar de.consejo: It is used with a noun or an infinitive: «a pesar del frío», «a pesar de estar cansado».
p.a pesar de que.consejo: It is used with a clause with a verb: «a pesar de que hace frío».
p.aun así.consejo: It marks a contrast with what came before: «llovía; aun así, salimos». It has no accent.
p.de todas formas.consejo: You can also say «de todos modos». It usually starts the sentence, with a comma.
p.sino.consejo: It corrects a negation: «no es rojo, sino azul». It is not the same as «si no».
p.sino que.consejo: Like «sino», but with a conjugated verb: «no estudia, sino que trabaja».
p.y eso que.consejo: It adds a surprising fact: «suspendí, y eso que estudié mucho».
p.excursión.consejo: It is written with x: eks-kur-SYON. It is feminine: «una excursión».
p.abrigo.consejo: It also means «shelter»: «al abrigo del viento». It is masculine: «el abrigo».
p.frío.consejo: The accent splits the i and the o: FRI-o. You say «hace frío» and «tengo frío».
p.nos mojamos.consejo: It comes from «mojarse». The j sounds like h: nos mo-HA-mos.
b1.texto:
**Aunque** can present a fact or a possibility. The verb mood tells how you see it:

- **Aunque está lloviendo**, salgo. (the rain is a fact)
- **Aunque llueva**, saldré. (I go out whether it rains or not)

**A pesar de** + noun or infinitive: a pesar del frío. **A pesar de que** + clause.

**Aun así** and **de todas formas** contrast with what came before. **Sino** corrects a negation: no es rojo, **sino** azul. With a conjugated verb: no estudia, **sino que** trabaja.
b2.f0.texto: Tomorrow we are going on the outing, even if it rains.
b2.f1.texto: Although I have a lot of work, I am coming with you.
b2.f2.texto: In spite of the cold, it is going to be fun.
b2.f3.texto: I am not taking an umbrella, but a coat.
b2.f4.texto: Last year we got very wet.
b2.f5.texto: Even so, we had a very good time.
b2.f6.texto: I fell in the mud, even though I was going slowly.
b2.f7.texto: Anyway, this time we are taking dry clothes.
b4.titulo: Aunque, a pesar de and sino
b4.texto:
- **aunque** + indicative: a fact → Aunque estoy cansado, voy.
- **aunque** + subjunctive: a possibility, or something that does not matter → Aunque llueva, iré.
- **a pesar de** + noun or infinitive → A pesar del frío, salimos. A pesar de estar cansado, voy.
- **a pesar de que** + clause → A pesar de que hace frío, iremos.
- **no… sino** corrects: No es rojo, **sino** azul.
- **no… sino que** + conjugated verb: No estudia, **sino que** trabaja.
b4.e0.texto: Although I am tired, I am coming with you.
b4.e1.texto: Even if it rains, I will go on the outing.
b4.e2.texto: He does not study; he works instead.
b5.f0.texto: The morning dawns cold and grey, with a low mist over the fields.
b5.f1.texto: Although the clouds hang heavy over the valley, the group leaves the village in good spirits.
b5.f2.texto: The rubber boots sound on the mud with a cheerful splashing.
b5.f3.texto: In spite of the fine rain, nobody complains about the slippery path.
b5.f4.texto: The drops shine on the bare branches like little crystals.
b5.f5.texto: At midday they reach a stone bridge over a green, fast river.
b5.f6.texto: They are not looking for a restaurant, but for a bench under the bridge.
b5.f7.texto: There, amid the smell of wet earth, they open their rucksacks and hand out sandwiches.
b5.f8.texto: Marta pours hot tea from an old flask into four metal cups.
b5.f9.texto: Anyway, the sun appears for a moment and paints the surface of the water gold.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! It is a possibility, not a fact: subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The indicative would present the rain as a sure fact.
b6.o2.refuerzo: With «aunque» the future is not used in this sentence.
b6.pregunta: I will go whether it rains or not. Which form is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: No: «aunque» says tiredness does not stop him.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! The tiredness is a fact, but it does not change his plan.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That would be the opposite of «voy».
b7.pregunta: «Aunque estoy cansado, voy». What does the speaker do?
b8.frase: Aun así lo pasamos muy bien
b8.traduccion: Even so, we had a very good time
b9.o0.refuerzo: After a negation that is corrected, Spanish uses «sino», not «pero».
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Aunque» means «although»; it does not fit here.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! «Sino» corrects what has been denied.
b9.pregunta: You correct a negation. Which word is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «A pesar de» + noun: «a pesar de la lluvia».
b10.o1.refuerzo: «A pesar de que» needs a clause with a verb.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Aunque» needs a verb after it, not just a noun.
b10.pregunta: A noun follows: «la lluvia». Which expression works?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «He does not study; he works instead».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «A pesar de» only works with a noun or an infinitive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «A pesar de que» introduces a clause with a verb.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The full expression has «de»: «a pesar de que».
b12.pregunta: A clause with a verb follows. What is missing?
p.divertido.consejo: From «divertirse», to have fun. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.barro.consejo: Wet earth that gets sticky. The «rr» between vowels is strong.
p.amanece.consejo: From «amanecer», to dawn. The «c» before «e» sounds like «th».
p.pesan.consejo: From «pesar», to weigh. Clouds that weigh look heavy and dark.
p.goma.consejo: Rubber, the material of boots. The «g» before «o» is hard.
p.chapoteo.consejo: The sound water makes when you step in it. Say «cha-po-TE-o».
p.queja.consejo: From «quejarse», to complain. «Nadie se queja» means nobody complains.
p.resbaladizo.consejo: Means slippery. The «z» sounds like «th» and the stress falls on «DI».
p.desnudas.consejo: Feminine plural of «desnudo». Here it describes branches without leaves.
p.mochilas.consejo: Plural of «mochila». The «ch» sounds like «ch» in «chico».
p.reparten.consejo: From «repartir», to share out. The initial «rr» is strong.
p.termo.consejo: A flask that keeps drinks hot. The stress falls on «TER».
p.superficie.consejo: The outer layer of something, like water. The «c» before «i» sounds like «th».
p.iremos.consejo: Future of «ir», for «nosotros». Here it means we will go anyway.
